title: Homemade Cinnamon Rolls (Cinnabon Copycat)

components.name: Dough
ingredients: 1/2 cup sourdough discard (optional but recommended — add alongside the butter)
directions: Pour warm milk into the bowl of a stand mixer and sprinkle yeast overtop. Allow to sit 3–4 minutes until slightly frothy.
Add eggs, butter, sourdough discard (if using), and sugar. Mix until combined.
Add salt and 4 cups of flour. Mix using the beater blade just until barely combined. Allow to rest 5 minutes.

Scrape off beater blade and attach dough hook. Beat on medium speed for 5–7 minutes, adding up to 1/2 cup more flour only if needed. Dough should be elastic, smooth, and tacky but pulling away from the bowl sides.
Spray a large bowl with cooking spray. Transfer dough and cover. Set in a warm place and let rise until doubled, about 30 minutes.

components.name: Filling
ingredients: 1/2 cup heavy cream (for pouring over risen rolls)
directions: While dough is rising, combine soft butter, brown sugar, and cinnamon until well combined. Set aside.
Sprinkle a work surface generously with flour. Turn out dough and roll to about a 24x15-inch rectangle.
Smooth the cinnamon filling over the whole dough rectangle with a rubber spatula.
Starting on the long side, roll up tightly jelly roll style. Cut into 12 slices and place in a greased 9x13 baking pan.
Cover and let rise for 20 minutes while oven preheats to 375°F.
Warm the heavy cream until the chill is off (not hot). Pour over the risen rolls.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until lightly golden brown and center rolls are cooked through. Check at 20 minutes; cover loosely with foil if browning too quickly.

components.name: Cream Cheese Frosting
directions: Blend cream cheese and butter with a hand mixer. Add powdered sugar and maple extract; beat until combined. Spread over cooled rolls.

notes: For overnight rolls: get to the second rise (rolled, cut, in pan), cover and refrigerate overnight. In the morning, let sit 30 minutes if risen, or 1 hour at room temperature if not, then pour on cream and bake. One yeast packet = 2 1/4 teaspoons.
